name: Lola Lowe
life: “I still remember my first kitchen's window over the biscuit works.” People around the brick passage off the shop row know Lola by a small Monday habit. Lola takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I asked to count it at the deli table. Behind a counter everybody starts looking like a suspect.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a red windbreaker and a train token tied to a zipper pull. Lola has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, with iron-gray waves. Lola turns fully toward the person speaking during a conversation.
personality: Lola enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To hold the count somewhere people can sit together.
family: Fiona Kelly is Lola’s first cousin once removed. Lola puts the kettle on. Fiona chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *A room above the dryers*, Fiona says, “I bought the first drawing with an installment plan.”
connections: Chris Anders. The deli-table count gives the worried owner a chance to recognize a familiar crease.

reactions.situation: A family asks to come back later without explanation
reactions.response: Lola arranges a second visit without repeating the family's explanation.
